claims.text: Post-fabrication deep cryogenic treatment improves the dimensional precision and mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
As-deposited laser-additively-manufactured HfNbTaTiZr or similar HEAs exhibit residual stresses.
As-deposited laser-additively-manufactured HfNbTaTiZr or similar HEAs contain non-equilibrium phases and fabrication-induced defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment can be applied as a post-processing step after laser additive manufacturing of an HEA.
The proposed treatment consists of prolonged immersion near -196°C, such as in liquid nitrogen.
An optimized cryogenic dwell can provide uniform treatment without thermal-shock damage.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines the grain structure of additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces a phase transition in laser-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr.
The induced transition produces beneficial HCP precipitates at grain boundaries.
Deep cryogenic treatment alleviates residual stresses in additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment promotes grain-boundary reorganization.
Residual-stress relief, grain-boundary reorganization, and phase transitions reduce internal defects.
Microstructural refinement improves dimensional stability by correcting distortion.
Microstructural refinement improves mechanical strength by minimizing defect-related stress concentrators.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases the tensile strength of laser-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr by 11% relative to the as-deposited state and by 25% relative to the as-cast state.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces dimensional distortion relative to untreated as-deposited components.
Deep cryogenic treatment lowers fabrication-induced defect density relative to untreated as-deposited components.
The expected benefit is greatest in alloys and geometries where residual stress and microstructural non-uniformity cause dimensional imprecision and mechanical weakness.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in dimensional precision, mechanical strength, and defect reduction relative to an untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
